title: Building a Seasonal Plate
excerpt: A good seasonal dish begins with a clear idea: one ingredient in focus, supporting flavours in balance and enough texture to make every bite interesting.
body: Every plate at Maison Élan starts with a single question: what is at its best right now? From there we choose one ingredient to lead and let everything else support it.

Balance comes next. A rich element wants acidity, a soft element wants crunch, and a sweet note is sharpened by something bitter or salty. We keep the plate uncluttered so each flavour can be tasted clearly.
Finally, texture. A scatter of toasted nuts, a crisp leaf or a spoonful of something silky is often what turns a good dish into a memorable one.

title: The Art of a Good Sauce
excerpt: A sauce should connect the elements of a plate. Acidity, texture and depth matter as much as richness, and a little restraint often makes the flavour clearer.
body: A sauce is the thread that ties a plate together. It should echo what is on the plate rather than compete with it.
We build ours slowly: good stock or cream as a base, a measured touch of acidity to lift it, and seasoning tasted at every stage.
Restraint matters. A spoonful that glosses the plate is usually better than a pool that drowns it.
